claims.summary: In [C5]'s real planar flow interpolation (its Lemma 2.10, flows f and h on the m x m grid with div f = div h and ||h||_inf <= U, g = h + rot grad of the McShane extension of the circulation's potential restricted off the set B where the maximal function of |p| exceeds U), g agrees with f off a set E_B of at most 4|B| <= 4L ||f||_2^2/U^2 edges; so for every u >= 0 the numbers of edges with load above u differ by at most that, and for every Phi >= 0, sum_e Phi(|g_e|) >= sum over e outside E_B of Phi(|f_e|). In [C5]'s setting (f electrical, U = LNRs), with probability tending to one, E_B is a fraction O((log N)^(-1/2)) of the edges, so at levels t <= (1/2 - eps) log log N the psi_4 counts of f and g agree up to a factor 1 + o(1), a failure by a factor 1 + delta transferring either way; above those levels neither direction is controlled, and every edge with |f_e| > U lies in E_B. The agreement is deterministic; only the size holds with probability tending to one. Not covered: the integral version (2.30), an optimal vertex of a linear program.
claims.assessment: Working proof: g - f = rot grad(psi~ - psi), which by [C5]'s proof of Lemma 2.9 vanishes off the edges incident to B, at most 4|B|, and [C5]'s (2.28) bounds |B|; the counts and the Orlicz inequality follow; the fraction from [C5]'s (2.3), (2.6) and (2.16), which hold with probability tending to one.
claims.rationale: Answers the queued item's interpolation reading inside a window of levels: there the interpolated flow's counts are the electrical flow's up to a factor 1 + o(1), and above it neither bounds the other. The item's other readings are decided: one level's counts by thm:per-level-count-matchings without flows, and at [C5]'s cell scale the flow bound's grid error 2hN(N^((K/(Lh))^4) - 1) rules out any flow there through lem:hopf-lax-matching-bound; at the conjecture's own grid a psi_4 flow is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy in flow form.
claims.next_action: Prove that the electrical flow of the cell excesses fails the psi_4 counts at a bounded level t > pi^2 L^4 on every grid where a central limit theorem applies, the conjecture's own grid included (normalized spread 1/(L sqrt(2 pi)) by the entry's heuristic), through a central limit theorem per edge and a second-moment bound on exceedance counts across log-correlated edges: a method refutation, deciding nothing about the cheapest flow.

relationships: The item it develops comes from that entry; the lemma concerns the electrical flow, which that theorem does not cover.
